locator.heading: Lungwort

source_text:
_Descript._] THIS is a kind of moss, that grows on sundry sorts of
trees, especially oaks and beeches, with broad, greyish, tough leaves
diversly folded, crumpled, and gashed in on the edges, and some spotted
also with many small spots on the upper-side. It was never seen to bear
any stalk or flower at any time.

_Government and virtues._] Jupiter seems to own this herb. It is of
great use to physicians to help the diseases of the lungs, and for
coughs, wheezings, and shortness of breath, which it cures both in man
and beast. It is very profitable to put into lotions that are taken to
stay the moist humours that flow to ulcers, and hinder their healing,
as also to wash all other ulcers in the privy parts of a man or woman.
It is an excellent remedy boiled in beer for broken-winded horses.

evidence.summary: Modern studies support the traditional use of Pulmonaria officinalis for respiratory ailments by demonstrating antioxidant properties that mitigate oxidative stress and potential antimicrobial activity against relevant pathogens, though clinical efficacy in humans remains to be fully established.

concordance.rationale: Modern evidence (PMID: 33530389, 28453265) demonstrates antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties in vitro. This pharmacological plausibility partially supports historical claims for respiratory ailments but lacks clinical trial data for curing coughs or ulcers.
concordance.uncertainty: High uncertainty due to absence of human clinical trials and reliance solely on in vitro/in silico studies.

issues: Unearned grade 'C': The concordance rationale cites in vitro evidence (PMID: 33530389, 28453265) as supporting pharmacological plausibility but explicitly notes the lack of clinical trial data. Assigning a grade based solely on in vitro findings for historical claims like 'curing coughs' is scientifically weak and arguably unearned given the high uncertainty flag.

Missing EMA evidence: The entry lists 'ema': false, yet no EMA approval or traditional medicinal product status was verified for Pulmonaria officinalis in the provided evidence, which is a standard completeness check for herbal entries.

Incomplete taxon resolution: While P. officinalis was selected, the other candidates (P. vulgaris, P. rubra) were not explicitly ruled out with specific botanical distinctions in the reasoning, relying only on 'LLM proposal' confidence scores.
